headline: Approved window restoration at 211 Bridge Street and façade work at 24 Congress Street; continued Charlotte Forten Park curfew and $20,000 grant request.
summary: The meeting covered a proposed sunset curfew for Charlotte Forten Park, which was continued to the November 4th meeting. A $20,000 grant request from Creative Collective was continued to the December 9th meeting. Approvals were given for window restoration at 211 Bridge Street and façade work at 24 Congress Street, both subject to Design Review Board review.
decisions: Continued the Charlotte Forten Park use policy and sunset curfew to the November 4th meeting, 4-0.
Continued the $20,000 Charlotte Forten Park grant request from Creative Collective to the December 9th meeting, 4-0.
Approved restoration of seven windows at 211 Bridge Street upon successful DRB review and subject to the DRB recommendation, 3-0.
Approved façade painting, tile trim, and new entry doors at 24 Congress Street pending DRB review and approval, 3-0.
Continued the Courthouse project financials and account reimbursement item to the November meeting, 3-0.
Approved the minutes of the three September 9th, 2026 meetings, 4-0.

SRA  
October 14, 2026 
Page 1 of 8 
 
City of Salem, Massachusetts 
Public Meeting Minutes 
 
Board or Committee: Salem Redevelopment Authority  
Date and Time:   Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 6:00pm 
Meeting Location:   Zoom Meeting  
SRA Members Present:  Chair Grace Napolitano, Christopher Dunn, Glenn Larose, 
and Ryan Macione 
SRA Members Absent: Christine Madore 
Others Present:  Tom Daniel, Executive Director, Kate Newhall-Smith, 
Principal Planner 
  
Executive Director’s Report 
 
Mr. Daniel reported October in Salem has been robust thus far.  
 
Mr. Daniel noted that that port terminal wind project is not proceeding due to the current federal 
administration, but the Commonwealth and Crowley are working for construction to commence for 
the port infrastructure. Legislation is pending that would provide for a phased approach to 
construction. He noted that are smaller cruise ships that would benefit from the construction of a 
deep-water berth.  
 
Mr. Daniel reported on the blue economy and climate technology. He said that Salem has been 
working with the Essex County Community Foundation, UMass Amherst, Gloucester Marine 
Station, North Shore Alliance for Economic Development, Mass Hire, North Middlesex Council of 
Governments, M3 Coalition, and others to collaborate in the climate tech space. This is part of the 
MA Leads Act and investments the state is looking to make in the climate tech industry and to be a 
global leader in this area. Two conferences have been held, and a third conference is planned for 
the spring.  
 
Charlotte Forten Park   
 
1. Review of Draft: Charlotte Forten Park Use Policy  
 
Assistant City Solicitor, Omar Bennani was present to discuss the proposed ordinance the 
Mayor’s team has for Charlotte Forten Park. 
• There were no policies in place prior to this proposed ordinance. The goal is to regulate the 
park.  
• The public has been raising concerns about some of the activities at the park. The Police 
Department said it would be easier for them to address activities if there were rules.  
• The SRA needs to weigh in on the sunset curfew, which would include every part of the park 
except for the Harbor Walk. Unless there is a permitted event, anyone could be removed 
from the park outside of the hours that are permitted.  
• Mr. Bennani noted that the park is essentially two lots. Lot 1 is retained by the City. Lot 2 is a 
20 ft wide strip of land that goes alongside the building at 285 Derby Street, which is the
SRA  
October 14, 2026 
Page 2 of 8 
 
easement area that was granted to the abutter for access to his building. The Harbor Walk 
is covered by a Chapter 91 license under the purview of the DEP.  
• DEP would need to approve the ordinance, hopefully as a minor modification as access 
would remain open to the Harbor Walk.  
• The goal is to ensure the City’s ordinance is aligned with the portion of the park owned by 
the SRA and the part owned by the City.  
• City Council has not approved the ordinance yet.  
• The request is for the SRA to vote to approve the ordinance as written contingent on City 
Council and DEP approval.  
• The SRA is voting first so that when City Council approves the ordinance, it’s not covering 
only 2/3 of the park. Also, due to timing of meetings, this is coming to the SRA before the 
Council.  
• Ms. Napolitano noted that the order of voting could be flipped in case the City Council 
wishes to make amendments.  
• Mr. Bennani confirmed that the language is based on an ordinance that covers Salem Com-
mon. 
• Mr. Bennani said the only component the SRA needs to consider is the curfew. His under-
standing is that the City Council has the authority to impose general conduct rules.  
• Ms. Napolitano noted that the City owns the majority of the park, so suggested that they 
should approve the language first.  
• Mr. Macione requested clarification of the rules that would apply or infringe upon the ease-
ment, and what land the SRA owns outside of the easement. 
• A plan showing the lot lines and easement was shared and reviewed.  
• The curfew ordinance would apply to members of the public on the easement. The ordi-
nance curfew would not apply to patrons of the businesses under the easement.  
• The curfew is the only language the SRA is being asked to approve.  
• Mr. Dunn expressed reticence in taking away someone’s right to walk through a public park 
and wanted to understand more of the reasons for the request.  
• Mr. Bennani reported that members of the public and area businesses have raised con-
cerns with overnight use of the park including encampments. The Police Department said 
that without anything to point to, such as an ordinance or signage, it is difficult for them to 
enforce anything in the park. The Mayor’s office would like to keep policies for this park in 
line with other City parks. A sunset curfew is a standard park regulation.  
• Mr. Dunn said he believes elected City officials should vote first if they are talking about a 
policy that would not permit someone in a park beyond dusk. He would also like to hear 
from public safety officials to hear that this is the right solution for the problem.  
• Mr. Bennani shared that the existing general conduct rules don’t prevent access to the 
park; those need to be set by the property owner.  
• Mr. Larose said he shares Mr. Dunn’s concern. He also expressed concern about how sun-
set is defined as it changes every day. Mr. Bennani said he agrees that having a more easily 
defined time is a good suggestion. Mr. Larose said he believes there needs to be more guid-
ance and deliberation of the City Council before the SRA votes.
SRA  
October 14, 2026 
Page 3 of 8 
 
• Mr. Dunn said it seems reasonable that the City Council and Mayor would want to have 
rules for parks for public safety and enforcement, but that it doesn’t seem reasonable to 
have different rules for different parks from a management perspective.  
• Ms. Napolitano said consistency across park regulations makes sense.  
• Mr. Bennani said his understanding is encampments have spurred these conversations. 
 
Russ Tanzer, 285 Derby Street, reported that they have had people camping on the easement 
area. He said the bulk of the encampments are on green areas of the park, but some have been 
on the hard surface, just before the Harbor Walk. He said there are hundreds of calls to the Po-
lice Department annually for the park. He said there have been assaults, public drinking, public 
nudity, bathing in the water fountain. He said there have been so many instances of drug over-
dose that the City installed a Narcan station in the park. He noted that it is a City-wide issue, 
and they are hoping the housing on Canal Street at Life Bridge will be able to provide decent, 
safe, and sanitary housing for these individuals. He said he sees these issues every day and 
complaints on websites reviewing businesses at 285 Derby Street; people are not feeling safe.  
 
John Andrews, Creative Collective, noted that is a systemic issue. He believes that the lack of 
activity and programming has been part of the challenge. He said he has set up security cam-
eras. He agrees with the sentiments that a curfew may not be the right solution and enforce-
ment could be difficult. He said there are good people there that are less fortunate and others 
that have difficult mental challenges. He said it’s been an issue in other city parks and public 
spaces.  
 
Russ Tanzer noted that the City Council is meeting to discuss changes to the ‘camping ordi-
nance’, which may impact what goes on at the park.  
 
• Ms. Napolitano recommended that Mr. Bennani come back to the SRA after the City Council 
has deliberated and voted on the language.  
• Mr. Dunn said he would like to have a representative from public safety at the meeting to 
learn about their approach to a solution and what enforcement would look like. He said he 
sympathizes with Mr. Andrews having to deal with these issues.  
• Ms. Newhall-Smith recommended the SRA take no action until the City Council vote. Mr. 
Bennani said they could continue it to the next meeting so that it stays on the agenda.  
 
VOTE: Dunn made a motion to continue until the November 4th meeting.  
Second: Macione.   
Roll Call: Dunn, Larose, Macione, and Napolitano. 4-0 in favor.  
 
2. Request for Grant Funding: Creative Collective is requesting $20,000 in Charlotte Forten Park 
funding to support its month-long Haunted Happenings activation activities.  
 
John Andrews with Creative Collective was present to discuss the request: 
• Ms. Newhall-Smith noted that the Board had the request and photos from the light 
installation.
SRA  
October 14, 2026 
Page 4 of 8 
 
• Mr. Andrews said the property has been interesting to manage but believes they are getting 
good feedback from the City and community.  
• He said there have been unexpected costs such as hiring overnight security and they need 
to invest in another generator due to power issues and the inability to power two food 
trucks. He has also had to hire someone for trash pick-up. He has also invested in 
marketing.  
• Mr. Andrews reported that they have gifted spaces to vendors to make sure the park is full.  
• He said his overall budget for the space is $56,000 and that he’ll end up roughly $12,000 
short at the end of the month and hopes that grant funding could be considered.  
• Mr. Andrew said he’s provided an extensive budget to Ms. Newhall-Smith. He said it is a 
difficult park to activate. 
• Mr. Macione thanked Mr. Andrews for his work and effort. He asked if food trucks normally 
provide their own power. Mr. Andrews said generators create noise and exhaust and it’s not 
the best method to operate. He said the power infrastructure is a challenge.  
• Mr. Andrews said they are trying to program every Thursday through Sunday with musicians, 
performers, live acts, and movies. He said Thursdays are not tourist heavy, so they are trying 
to provide programming that appeals to locals which has incurred additional costs.  
• Mr. Andrews pays a percentage of the vendor fee revenue to the City per the RFP .  
• Expected fees to the City will likely be $3,000-$4,000.  
• Mr. Larose felt that $20,000 was a large sum given the finite nature of the resource. He was 
pleased to hear of the programming geared towards locals.  He would be open to supporting 
a smaller request.  
• Mr. Andrews estimates ten vendors a day at $175 each. He also has sponsorship money.  
• Mr. Dunn said he’s having a hard time justifying the request. Mr. Andrews said he knows that 
Anthem received funding last year. He said this will not be a huge revenue generator. Mr. 
Dunn said he needed to see a full accounting of revenue before voting to approve any 
funding.  
• Mr. Daniel said he has already granted Mr. Andrews $5,000 per his delegated authority to do 
so. That funding went towards trying to offset some of the cost of the canopy lighting. He 
said the City has taken different approaches to Haunted Happenings and vendor 
management and fee structure/revenue.  
• Mr. Daniel said the easement area is the only property the SRA owns and that the rest of the 
park is owned by the City. The sale of the easement to 285 Derby Street is what funded the 
activation account.  
• Mr. Dunn reiterated that he wasn’t comfortable with a vote to approve the funding, 
especially given it is a one-time funding source without a way to replenish. He added that it 
may make sense for the applicant to communicate his financial concerns to the City since 
the City is benefitting, in part, from the one-day licenses and revenue share.  
• Mr. Daniel added that the City has tremendous costs during the month of October for DPS, 
police, etc.  
• Mr. Andrews said he would be happy to share his revenue budget next month. He said the 
management of the park is a 24/7 operation and there have been unexpected side effects.  
• Mr. Andrews noted that he is not permitted to have temporary signage due to the building 
department’s rules and had to invest in a pod to put a temporary sign on that.
SRA  
October 14, 2026 
Page 5 of 8 
 
• He hopes to be part of the conversation to figure out how to make the park successful in the 
future.  
• Ms. Newhall-Smith noted that Anthem received a larger grant to support programming 
between Christmas and New Year’s, as well as funding last October to hide the 
construction fence around the shade structure. Their contract was two years.  
 
Russ Tanzer, 285 Derby Street, noted that Mr. Andrews is doing a good job at the park and that it 
is well managed and nice to see activity at the park.  
 
VOTE: Dunn made a motion to continue until the December 9th meeting.  
Second: Larose.   
Roll Call: Dunn, Larose, Macione, and Napolitano. 4-0 in favor.  
 
Projects in the Urban Renewal Area  
 
1. 211 Bridge Street: Small Project Review – Restoration of seven windows on the southern fa-
çade. 
 
Dale Yale was present to discuss the proposal: 
• Ms. Yale noted that they are working to restore seven windows at the Salem Playhouse and 
require approval from the SRA and Historic Commission.  
• The Salem Playhouse received $52,000 in CPA funds to restore the windows that face the 
courtyard and Federal Street.  
• The Playhouse has retained Window Women of New England and architect Ray Gurton to 
participate in the project.  
• A rendering and plan of the façade was shared.  
• Window Women will be removing the windows and restoring them offsite under the over-
sight and direction of Mr. Gurton.  
• The work includes replacing all exterior and interior wood jam trim, sills, moldings, and 
painting.  
• The Historic Commission has approved the work.  
• The work also requires approval of the DRB. Construction is expected to start in the spring. 
• The building is located in the B5 Central Business District, which is an important entrance 
to the City. The SRA holds a façade easement on the building.  
• The building is also listed on the National Register of Historic Places and the Massachu-
setts Historical Commission holds a preservation easement on the building. 
• The restoration is necessary to protect and preserve the building and safeguard it from fur-
ther weather-related deterioration and improve energy efficiency.  
• The Old Essex Stage Company regularly uses the building for rehearsals and stage produc-
tions.  
• Mr. Larose said it is a great proposal and that everything appears to be in order and is con-
sistent with guidance for this type of project.  
 
There were no comments or questions from members of the public.
SRA  
October 14, 2026 
Page 6 of 8 
 
 
VOTE: Larose made a motion to approve the project upon successful completion of DRB review 
and subject to the DRB recommendation subsequently issued.   
Second: Macione.   
Roll Call: Dunn, Larose, and Macione. 3-0 in favor.  
 
2. 24 Congress Street: Small Project Review – Façade painting, installation of tile trim, and new 
entry doors for Mexizol.  
 
Chef Eddie Diaz was present to discuss this proposal: 
• Mr. Diaz said they are looking to change the color and replace the front doors.  
• They would like to propose a green color for the outside with light cream and tileaccents. 
The windows will remain.  
• A rendering and proposed colors were shared.  
• There are no proposed changes to the brick.  
 
Russ Tanzer said they are delighted that Mexizol is coming to Salem and that they do an amaz-
ing job. He is excited to have a refresh of the building along Congress Street.  
 
VOTE: Macione made a motion to approve the project pending DRB review and approval.  
Second: Larose.   
Roll Call: Dunn, Larose, and Macione. 3-0 in favor.  
 
New/Old Business  
1. FY 2027 Goals 
 
• Ms. Newhall-Smith noted that the Board looked at the annual goals at the last meeting 
and then followed up with SRA members on revisions. The revised document, with track 
changes, was posted on SharePoint.  
• Changes were made to the organizational goal and methods of sharing information, 
staff enforcement, City enforcement, City initiatives, and best practices for micro-grant 
applications for Charlotte Forten Park.  
• A final goal was to consider looking at an annual or biannual meeting with economic de-
velopment and historic preservation partners that work downtown.  
• The language relating to Charlotte Forten Park was reviewed. 
 
VOTE: Dunn made a motion to approve the FY 2027 Goals.  
Second: Larose.   
Roll Call: Dunn, Larose, Macione, and Napolitano. 4-0 in favor.  
 
2. SRA Financials  
a. Courthouse Project Financials and Account Reimbursement 
• Ms. Newhall-Smith requested that this item be continued to the next meeting.
SRA  
October 14, 2026

VOTE: Larose made a motion to continue until the November meeting.  
Second: Macione.   
Roll Call: Larose, Macione, and Napolitano. 3-0 in favor. (Dunn stepped away from the meeting 
and did not vote on this item) 
 
b. General finances 
3. Other  
 
Mr. Daniel provided an update on the Courthouse project. He said that since the closing, it 
has been internal housekeeping items with Winn such as making sure insurance is set up. 
Winn Is hoping to submit their Building Permit for Phase 1 in the coming weeks. Construc-
tion fencing will be installed inside the granite wall at that time. Winn is working with the 
Public Art Planner to do some public art on the fence. They are waiting on a report to see if 
the elevator can be salvaged or if it needs to be completely refurbished.  
 
In regard to the Exchange, there is groundwork to be done and concrete is being poured. In 
the next month, aboveground work should start.  
 
A preview to the finances is the administrative services fee the SRA received for providing 
services during construction, which will be roughly $12,500 once a month and will go into 
the SRA’s general account.  
 
More information on the occupancy of the National Guard is expected in another month.  
 
Mr. Dunn inquired about the City Council liaison to the SRA. Mr. Daniel said the City Coun-
cil organizes liaisons. Mr. Dunn said it may make sense to reignite that role if the ordinance 
issues at Charlotte Forten Park comes back.  
 
Ms. Newhall-Smith said she is working with Ms. Owens to meet with local artists who do 
window art to understand their process and financial and time inputs. They hope to get per-
spectives from the artists and business owners after October. She said the artists they have 
met with have been wonderful and have been open to looking at ideas for draft language. 
She said she doesn’t see this item coming back before the SRA until December at the earli-
est.  
 
Approval of Minutes  
1. September 9, 2026  
a) Joint Public Meeting with the SRA  
b) Regular Meeting  
c) Annual Meeting  
 
VOTE: Dunn made a motion to approve the minutes of the three meetings held on September 9th.  
Second: Macione 
Roll Call: Dunn, Larose, Macione, and Napolitano. 4-0 in favor.

October 14, 2026

Adjournment  of Regular Meeting  
 
VOTE: Macione made a motion to adjourn the regular meeting.   
Seconded by: Dunn 
Roll Call: Dunn, Larose, Macione, and Napolitano. 4-0 in favor.
